sections.html:
Three routes lead to a sale: an agent listing, a sale by owner, or a cash offer. Of the three, the buyer with no lender is typically the fastest. Buckeye has nearly 30 master-planned communities in play, so find out early whether yours adds rules or fees to a sale.

  • Ask whether your community has an HOA, a community facilities district or a transfer fee, and collect the documents.
  • Get every buyer's closing date and seller-cost list in writing.
  • Keep copies of permits for pools, solar, fences and additions.

Buckeye had an estimated 125,445 residents on July 1, 2025, a 37.1 percent jump from 91,502 in April 2020. Owner-occupants hold 86.0 percent of the housing, at a median value of $419,800.

Occupied master-planned communities include Verrado, Sundance, Tartesso, Festival Ranch, Sienna Hills, Westpark and Riata West. Others, such as Teravalis, which is planned for nearly 300,000 residents, are still unbuilt.

Skyline Regional Park, an 8,700 acre mountain preserve in the southern White Tank Mountains, and Buckeye Hills Regional Park, seven miles south of downtown on State Route 85, are the large outdoor draws. If your home is near either, say so in the listing. Several school districts serve the city, and the one for your address should be confirmed before you mention schools in a listing.

Start with the city's Permit Center, part of Development Services. The department's phone number is 623-349-6200. The city warns that scammers send fake invoices from addresses ending in @usa.com, while the official domain is @buckeyeaz.gov. If an invoice for a permit or fee shows up unexpectedly, confirm it by phone before paying.

Ask the Permit Center whether a past project on your property, such as a pool, patio cover, solar panels or fence, was permitted and closed out. Ask the Business Licenses office what applies to renting the house before you sell, including the transaction privilege tax license questions on its Residential Rental Properties FAQ page. For nightly rentals, ask what the city requires at your address.

  • Find out whether past pool, solar, fence or patio work was permitted and closed.
  • Learn which rental licenses apply if you lease before you sell.
  • Verify any unexpected invoice by phone before you pay it.

sections.h2: Taxes and recording for a Buckeye sale
sections.html:
Buckeye is in Maricopa County, so the Maricopa Treasurer bills your property taxes, usually in two installments. A.R.S. 42-18052 sets the schedule: October 1 for the first half, with delinquency after November 1, then the following March 1 for the second, with delinquency after May 1. Pay the entire year by December 31 and no interest is added. If a mortgage company pays your taxes, check that the next installment is covered before closing.

Most documents cost $30 to record with the Maricopa County Recorder. The Arizona Department of Revenue requires an Affidavit of Property Value with a deed unless an A.R.S. 11-1134 exemption applies, and exempt deeds carry a notation such as A.R.S. 11-1134 B3. Owners who think the valuation is wrong can appeal to the county assessor within 60 days of the Notice of Value.

A copy of a recorded document is $1 a page, and a certified one adds $3 per document. After closing, have your title company order the recorded deed for you. It shows the date and the parcel number.

sections.h2: What a sale looks like step by step
sections.html:
The sequence is short once the paperwork is in hand. You gather HOA or community documents and permit copies. You collect offers with closing dates and seller costs in writing. You sign with one buyer, and the title company checks the Maricopa County tax balance, prepares the deed and the Affidavit of Property Value, and records the deed. Cash buyers skip the wait for loan approval, which is where most of the time is saved.

If your community has a transfer fee or a community facilities district, ask for the documents now. Pulling them together early helps you hold to the closing date you agreed on. If a mortgage company pays your taxes, that is one more place a payoff or a paid-through date has to be confirmed before closing.

sections.h2: Selling a house with taxes owed
sections.html:
Open the Maricopa County Treasurer's parcel lookup before you list and note which installments are paid. Anything still open gets paid from your proceeds at closing, and the title company will ask for the balance. Tell the title company early if a mortgage servicer is paying the taxes, since the next installment has to be covered before closing. The December 31 date matters here: a seller who closes in the fall can either clear the full year first or leave the first-half balance for escrow to settle.

Property tax isn't the only bill to check. If you rented the house, confirm your rental licenses are current, and ask the Business Licenses office about the transaction privilege tax questions on its Residential Rental Properties FAQ page.

Buckeye is hot desert, and an inspector will look hard at the roof and the cooling system. Have the age of both on hand, along with receipts for any service. If you sell as-is, expect the price to reflect what an inspection finds, and ask each cash buyer whether the offer changes after they walk through.

sections.h2: Where homes sit in the city
sections.html: Buckeye is large, about 393 square miles, and the westernmost suburb of the Phoenix area. The old downtown is built around Monroe Avenue, and Watson Road is the commercial center. Newer homes sit in the master-planned communities spread across the rest of the city. A downtown bungalow and a house in a planned community can play by different rules, from HOA dues to who maintains the common areas, so describe yours to buyers with its rules attached.

sections.h2: What to hand your title company
sections.html: Bring the deed, copies of permits, any HOA or community facilities district paperwork, and the latest Maricopa County tax statement. Add the payoff figure if a mortgage remains. The title company turns these into the closing statement, the deed and the Affidavit of Property Value, and it records the deed with the Maricopa County Recorder. Seller costs should match the list you got from the buyer in writing. If a number on the statement differs from that list, ask why before signing.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Buckeye?
faqs.a: The median value of an owner-occupied home is $419,800 for 2020 to 2024. The median gross rent over the same period was $1,963.

faqs.q: When are Maricopa County property taxes due for a Buckeye home?
faqs.a: The first half is due October 1 and delinquent after November 1. The second half is due March 1 and delinquent after May 1. Paying the full year by December 31 avoids interest.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed for a Buckeye sale?
faqs.a: The Maricopa County Recorder charges $30 for most documents. A completed Affidavit of Property Value or an exemption notation on the deed has to accompany it.

faqs.q: Which phone number should I use for Buckeye permit questions?
faqs.a: The city's Development Services department answers at 623-349-6200. Confirm any invoice or fee with that number before paying it.

faqs.q: What should I ask about before selling in a master-planned community?
faqs.a: Ask whether the community has an HOA, a community facilities district or a transfer fee, and collect the documents. Buyers will want to see them, and they may add costs to the sale.
